samples.title: Synthetic power corridor (known answers)
samples.description: A scene generated by scripts/make_synthetic_corridor.py: sloping terrain, 30 trees, 2 buildings, 3 towers, two spans of three phase conductors plus a shield wire, a low distribution line and 300 outliers. It is NOT a scan. The file carries no classification and states its units (metres) in the LAS header. The generator also writes the exact wire geometry, so detection and clearance results can be checked against known answers.
samples.provenance: Created by Neo Forge Technology for this demonstration; no third-party data. Free to use.
does_not_demonstrate: behaviour on real scanner noise, occlusion and sparsity

samples.title: San Francisco residential block (USGS 3DEP, real airborne lidar)
samples.description: A 120 m x 120 m tile of USGS 3D Elevation Program airborne lidar (project CA_SanFrancisco_1_B23) around 37.756 N, 122.4905 W, cut from the public Entwine/EPT copy and written in UTM zone 10N (EPSG:32610) so horizontal distances are true metres (the EPT copy itself is in Web Mercator, which stretches horizontal distances by about 1.27 here). Units (metres) are stated in the file header. Dense (about 110 points per m2), ground and noise labelled by the data provider (classes 2, 1, 7), no RGB. USGS did not classify wires in this project, so it carries no wire labels.
samples.provenance: USGS 3DEP lidar point cloud, project CA_SanFrancisco_1_B23, https://registry.opendata.aws/usgs-lidar/ ; cut and reprojected with services/lidar-wires/scripts/fetch_usgs_tile.py
samples.licence: US Government work, public domain (USGS 3DEP data carry no use restrictions); credit: USGS 3D Elevation Program
demonstrates: loading and rendering real airborne lidar
does_not_demonstrate: verified wire detection: whether any wires appear in this tile is shown by the detector's own output, which is unverified
